answer: Skip-gram is equivalent to optimizing a classification (matrix factorization) loss over adjacency matrices when the negative-sampling approximation is replaced by the full softmax/exact objective: i.e., when every (word, context) pair in the entire vocabulary is treated as a training example, with the full co-occurrence (adjacency) matrix of the graph or corpus used as the target, rather than sampling a few negative words per positive pair. In that setting the loss is a weighted cross-entropy over all node pairs (a dense classification of whether each pair is connected), which is the form studied in graph embedding analyses such as the connection between DeepWalk/skip-gram and matrix factorization of the random-walk co-occurrence matrix (Qiu et al., 2018). Negative sampling is used in practice for computational tractability, since the full softmax over a large vocabulary is expensive.
